schemeScope: Combined Paper 1 and Paper 2 scheme. PDF 18 reading marking instructions; 19–22 Léamhthuiscint A; 23–26 Léamhthuiscint B; 27 the Gaeilge 5 note, the general notes note, 2A and its Eolas/Gaeilge table; 27–30 prose (2B’s table after its marking-panel note); 31–35 poetry; 36 Ceist 4 instructions, 4A and its Eolas/Gaeilge table; 36–43 additional literature; 44 modified marking (SMM). reviewMethod: Every paper page and every applicable scheme page read in the text layer and checked against the printed page; each reading prompt, scheme slice, literature prompt and band table is asserted against the PDFs by the builder.

nonPoolDecisions: Reading (2019: Léamhthuiscint A and B both compulsory): all twelve questions of both passages are carded as whole questions; each printed part is also a practice card at its published tariff. 2019 prices no part “1 mharc + 1 mharc”, so there are no one-mark answer slots; “2 mharc + 1 mharc” items (A1(a), A2(a), A4(a), A5(a), B1(a), B3(a), B4(a), B5(a) and both 6(a)) stay whole as 0/2/3.

A 6(b) prices two independent six-mark traits (trait 2 + example 4) and B 6(b) two independent six-mark reasons (reason 2 + discussion 4); each half is also a practice slot. Both must be in the candidate’s own words.
Single-answer parts allow only the mark values the scheme prints for them (0, the printed partials and the full tariff).
Prose, poetry and Q4 choices are closed printed routes (2 + 2 + 6), each one card; the optional short story or poem itself is open content chosen inside one route.
sourceFindings: Paper 2 = 200: Ceist 1 Léamhthuiscint A 50 and B 50 (Q1–5 at 7 = (a) 3 + (b)(i) 2 + (b)(ii) 2; Q6 at 15 = (a) 3 + (b) 12); Ceist 2 Prós 30 (2A or 2B); Ceist 3 Filíocht 30 (3A or 3B); Ceist 4 Litríocht Bhreise 40 (one of 4A–4F).
Reading A “Constance Markievicz” (paper 4–5, scheme PDF 19–22); B “Taighde agus Taiscéalaíocht sa Spás” (paper 6–7, scheme PDF 23–26).

Literature language: 5 marks for Gaeilge in every literature answer (scheme PDF 27); prose 25 Eolas; poetry printed (i) 15, (ii) 6, (iii) 9 on the paper, assessed as Eolas 13, 5, 7 plus Gaeilge 5 once; Q4 Eolas 35; 4F (Colmáin) printed (i) 20, (ii) 10, (iii) 10, assessed as Eolas 19, 7, 9 (two points, 5 + 4) plus Gaeilge 5.

Text layer: the prose and Q4 band tables print the Eolas and Gaeilge columns side by side; 2A’s (PDF 27) and 4A’s (PDF 36) sit inside the answer, 2B’s follows its marking-panel note (PDF 30), and 2A’s and 2B’s copies differ by one full stop, so each prose card carries its own. 3A(i) prints its own “Cur síos (13 mharc)” table in place and stores (ii)’s Marc as 4 table after the panel note on PDF 32; 3B prints Marc as 11 and Marc as 4 in place; 4F stores (ii)’s Marc as 7 table after (iii)’s notes. The builder returns each table to the sub-question it prices and ends each answer at the panel note.
4A prints a reduction for an answer that discusses only one character (“Duine amháin luaite agus pléite … Eolas (35-10) (25) =”), lifted inside 4A’s Eolas guidance.
B 6(b): the scheme prints its tariff as “Dhá chúis = 6 mharc + 6 mharc”, not in the braces used for every other reading part.
No legacy cards exist for 2019 Higher Paper 2: every card is new, with IDs in the 2020–2026 pattern.

Scheme misprints, kept as printed: the Ceist 4 marking-panel note on PDF 43 says “an marc as 25 (Eolas)” although Ceist 4 is Eolas 35 (its panel prints “Eolas (35) =”); 3A(iii) prints “Ainm an file = Máirtín Ó Direáin = 1 mharc”. The note is the answer’s boundary and is not carried on any card.
